assumptions.note: The house runs on Sydney's observed weather and NSW1 spot prices whatever the address. Prices and solar are forecast by models trained on data before 1 Dec 2025. For a fair test, the models are only shown periods they never saw, so they were trained once and not updated since. In a working system they would be retrained regularly on newer data, so forecasts this far past their training data would be more accurate.
assumptions.tariff: Imports pay the NSW1 spot price plus Ausgrid's network charge (35.8 c/kWh 3-9 pm in summer and winter, 5.9 c/kWh otherwise) plus GST; exports earn the spot price; $1.10/day supply.

warnings: For this house, the battery's own self-consumption mode did better than the planner over this window, by $1.59 once battery wear is counted. Planning has little to work with when the house can't export or the battery is small for its solar and demand.
Payback takes 11.2 years, longer than the usual 10-year battery warranty.

payback.basis: 14 weeks spread over 1 Dec 2025 - 18 Sep 2026, scaled to a year. The models never saw any of it. It covers 10 of 12 months; the rest of the year is assumed to be like them.
payback.cost_sources: Typical 2026 installed prices: solar about $0.83/W in NSW after the STC rebate (Solar Choice price index); batteries $650-$1,100/kWh before rebates. Federal Cheaper Home Batteries rebate at the May-Dec 2026 rate ($272/kWh for the first 14 kWh, 60% to 28 kWh, 15% to 50 kWh).
